The api died because the disk filled up: the `report-export` job filled `/var/lib/stockroom`, the database could no longer write, and the api exited at 03:14:06 and never came back.

Starting at 03:05:00, `report-export` wrote a 512 MB CSV into `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` every 12 seconds, 40 files (about 20 GB) by 03:12:48. The disk warned at 91% at 03:09:03 and 99% at 03:13:30. At 03:14:00 the db logged `could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device`, the api aborted its transaction, shut down its worker pool and exited with `FATAL api: exiting (status 1)`.

From 03:16:00 the proxy logged `upstream api refused connection` every two minutes through 05:28:00, just before the log ends at 05:29:57. There is no api restart anywhere in the log, so the api was still down when the log ends, while web and proxy requests kept returning 200.

The `cache: slow command` warnings (100–150 ms) recur every five minutes or so both before and after the crash, so they look unrelated.

To recover, free space in `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` and then restart the api. To stop a repeat, move the exports off the database's volume or cap what the job writes.

The log's timestamps are all 2026-03-09, not last night, so check that this is the right file for the outage you mean.
